Install and configure the privileged Rugix Ctrl daemon.

## Inputs

No artifact inputs.

## Parameters

<dl class="parameter-list">

<dt>

`dangerously_insecure`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `false`

Bypass normal daemon authorization checks.

</dd>

<dt>

`factory_reset`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `false`

Allow daemon clients to request a factory reset.

</dd>

<dt>

`system_commit`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `false`

Allow daemon clients to commit a trial system.

</dd>

<dt>

`system_reboot`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `false`

Allow daemon clients to reboot the system.

</dd>

<dt>

`app_lifecycle`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `false`

Allow daemon clients to manage application lifecycle operations.

</dd>

</dl>

## Scheduling

| Setting      | Value        |
| ------------ | ------------ |
| Priority     | `100000`     |
| Dependencies | `rugix-ctrl` |

Higher priorities run first within the selected recipe set unless `before` or
`after` constraints require otherwise. Dependencies include other recipes
without ordering them.

## Behavior

Requires systemd and a Rugix Ctrl release that provides daemon mode. The recipe
installs its service and access configuration. Each capability is disabled by
default; enable the operations required by the clients that will use the daemon.

## Example

For example, add the recipe to a layer derived from a compatible base:

```toml
recipes = ["core/rugix-ctrl-daemon"]
```
